# pbs_node_config (Resource)

Manages the settings of a Proxmox Backup Server node, which it keeps in `node.cfg`: the HTTP proxy, the sender of its mail, how long it keeps task logs, the default language, the TLS ciphers of its proxy, the consent banner, its notes and its location. The web interface shows the proxy, the sender, the language, the consent text and the location under **Configuration → Other → General**, and the notes on the node's **Notes** page; the task logs and the ciphers are set through the API or `proxmox-backup-manager node update` only.

The node is a singleton, and the resource manages only the settings its configuration sets: one it leaves out is neither read nor changed, and keeps whatever the node has. Creating the resource writes the settings it sets over the node's; removing a setting from the configuration, or destroying the resource, deletes the settings it managed, so that PBS goes back to its defaults for them. The ACME settings of the same file belong to `pbs_node_acme`, and this resource never touches them; both write with the file's digest, so that neither overwrites the other.

Reading the settings needs `Sys.Audit on /system`, changing them `Sys.Modify on /system`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The node's settings in node.cfg. Settings left out keep whatever the node
# has; removing one from here later deletes it.
resource "pbs_node_config" "this" {
  email_from        = "pbs@example.net"
  task_log_max_days = 90
  default_lang      = "en"

  # PBS checks updates, the subscription and webhooks through the proxy.
  http_proxy = "http://proxy.example.net:3128"

  # Shown on the login page; everyone must accept it before signing in.
  consent_text = <<-EOT
    **Authorised use only.** Activity on this server is logged.
  EOT

  description = <<-EOT
    # Backup server for cluster1
    Offsite copy: pbs2.example.net
  EOT

  # PBS 4.2.1 or later.
  location = {
    name      = "Vienna"
    latitude  = 48.2082
    longitude = 16.3738
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `ciphers_tls_1_2` (String) OpenSSL cipher list the proxy offers for TLS 1.2, such as `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`, instead of OpenSSL's defaults for Mozilla's intermediate configuration. PBS refuses a list that matches no cipher. The proxy reads it only when it starts, reloads (`systemctl reload proxmox-backup-proxy`) or loads a new certificate, so a change takes effect then. `@SECLEVEL=N` above 2 applies to the proxy's certificate chain too, and a chain with weaker keys then keeps the proxy from starting: the plan warns. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `ciphers_tls_1_3` (String) OpenSSL cipher suites the proxy offers for TLS 1.3, such as `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`. OpenSSL skips names it does not know, so check the spelling. Like `ciphers_tls_1_2`, it takes effect when the proxy next starts, reloads or loads a certificate. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `consent_text` (String) Text of a consent banner that everyone must accept on the login page before signing in, in Markdown, up to 49152 bytes. The provider stores it in PBS base64-encoded, as the web interface does. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `default_lang` (String) Language of the web interface in a browser where no language was chosen in the interface — on the login page or with its Language button, which keep the choice in a cookie; PBS does not go by the browser's own language. One of `ar`, `ca`, `da`, `de`, `en`, `es`, `eu`, `fa`, `fr`, `gl`, `he`, `hu`, `it`, `ja`, `kr`, `nb`, `nl`, `nn`, `pl`, `pt_BR`, `ru`, `sl`, `sv`, `tr`, `zh_CN`, `zh_TW`; PBS shows English when the language's translation is not installed. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `description` (String) Notes on the node, in Markdown, as the **Notes** page of the web interface shows and edits them; lines end in `\n`, and tabs are allowed, but no other control characters. PBS stores each line as a comment line of `node.cfg` and reads the notes back ending in a line break, so a line break at the end, or its absence, is no change; the provider sends them with one, which older PBS needs for a line with a tab. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `email_from` (String) Address the node's mail comes from: the notifications of sendmail endpoints that set no `from_address`, `mail-to-root` included. Without it, PBS sends them from `root`. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `http_proxy` (String, Sensitive) HTTP proxy PBS connects through to the internet, `[http://][user:password@]host[:port]`, such as `http://proxy.example.org:3128`; without a port, PBS uses 1080. PBS uses it for the subscription check, notifications to Gotify and webhooks, and the S3 endpoints and remotes that set `use_node_proxy` — from PBS 4.1.7 to 4.2.3, every S3 endpoint, whatever it sets —, and writes it to APT's configuration, `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/76pveproxy` — anew whenever the node's settings change, and removing the file when there is no proxy. PBS's ACME client does not use it: ordering and renewing a certificate (`pbs_node_certificate`, `pbs_node_certificate_renew`, PBS's daily update) needs a direct connection to the CA. Sensitive, as it may hold a password, which PBS returns. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.
- `location` (Attributes) Where the node is, which PBS shows on a map. PBS 4.2.1 or later. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--location))
- `node` (String) Node whose settings to manage: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`. PBS is a single node, so both name the same settings: manage them with one resource only. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `task_log_max_days` (Number) Days PBS keeps the logs of finished tasks, which it rotates every night. Without it, PBS keeps the last 20 rotated archives, of about 512 KiB each, however old. Leaving it out leaves the node's setting alone; removing it from the configuration deletes the setting.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `node`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

<a id="nestedatt--location"></a>
### Nested Schema for `location`

Required:

- `latitude` (Number) Latitude in degrees, from -90 to 90.
- `longitude` (Number) Longitude in degrees, from -180 to 180.

Optional:

- `name` (String) Name of the place, such as `Vienna`, without commas: PBS would write one into `node.cfg` unquoted, and could not read the file again.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_node_config.this
  identity = {
    node = "localhost"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `node` (String) Node name, such as `localhost`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_node_config.this
  id = "localhost"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The settings of a node are imported by the node's name. An import manages
# every setting the node has: a plan deletes those the configuration leaves
# out.
terraform import pbs_node_config.this localhost
```
